blocks.title: Greedy algorithm
blocks.text: A greedy algorithm makes a sequence of choices, each locally optimal, hoping they lead to a globally optimal solution. It is often used when a problem has optimal substructure: the optimal solution can be built from optimal solutions to its subproblems.

Coin change: to make an amount with the fewest coins, repeatedly take the largest coin that does not exceed the remaining amount and subtract it, until the amount is reached. Greedy algorithms are often faster and easier to implement than other techniques, but they do not always give the optimal answer, so check that the greedy approach fits the problem (Tip).
